ladder_analysis.why: Every operation is deterministic and exhaustively testable. The season switch is a date comparison, August 21 is either past or it is not (c14), same for the restaurant window (c16) and the aurora amenity window (c19). Which property a clerk stands in is a setting, not an inference (c4). The van group exclusion is written policy applied as a rule (c18). Deciding the one correct answer per question is editorial work the company must own, not a modelling problem. It fixes a defect visible from outside before any model exists (c14 versus c19). Google Rule of ML one applied literally.
ladder_analysis.what_the_next_rung_up_would_have_to_earn: Nothing. This rung is the floor and it clears the bar by itself.

ladder_analysis.why: As specced it is a generative RAG assistant. The GENERATION step is the part that is not earned. Over a corpus this small the genuine gap a rules search leaves is vocabulary, a first-week clerk types the guest's words while the card is titled in the company's words. That is a matching problem, and matching is the retrieval rung. The composite question does not earn generation either, because the composition axes are bounded, three properties (c4), two seasons (c14, c16, c19), air or rail (c17), group or individual (c18). Recurring composites are authorable as scenario cards, which are testable, auditable and in the company's voice. A model-composed answer is none of those. Rare composites should escalate to the 24/7 desk (c12), which is the correct answer for rare and consequential.
ladder_analysis.what_the_next_rung_up_would_have_to_earn: Generation would have to be earned by a phase-one query log showing a real, repeating population of questions that no authored card and no card combination serves, where the clerk searched, got relevant cards, and still escalated. Absent that log the generation layer is a preference, not a requirement.
ladder_analysis.downscope_to: Desk Search. Semantic matching over the canonical cards that returns the card itself, VERBATIM, top three, with property and season applied as deterministic pre-filters. No generated prose, no dictation in v1, an explicit no-match path that names the supervisor. AI role thin, ONE model-touched step. Funded only after the phase-one log shows the gap is real.

ladder_analysis.why: A shared dispatch board plus a structured form gets most of this with zero AI. The group exclusion is stated policy (c18), the van already runs 24 hours (c17), and the desk is already staffed 24 hours by design (c12), so there is no unattended window, which is the usual justification for anything conversational here.
ladder_analysis.what_the_next_rung_up_would_have_to_earn: A thin parsing node would have to be earned by structured intake actually failing in production. Nobody has that number and nobody outside the company can get it.

ladder_analysis.why: The variable content in a first response is availability and price, and the design already leaves both as human-filled blanks. Everything else is static property description. A snippet library and a merge template gets most of the value with no model and no risk. Evidence base is one homepage sentence (c2) and one routing line (c1), and the analogue is a vendor press release whose named first pilot reports no baseline and no numbers at all (c41).
ladder_analysis.what_the_next_rung_up_would_have_to_earn: Inbound enquiries proving too varied for templates, which requires enquiry volume and current first-response time, a measurement only the company can make.
ladder_analysis.downscope_to: Not a build. ONE question asked in the first conversation, enquiry volume and current first-response time on the published path (c1, c2, c3). Held in Next, not scoped and not priced until that number exists.

cost_of_error_headline.the_sharpest_objection: The human in the loop is PARTLY A COMFORTABLE STORY. The reviewer is by design a first-week seasonal hire (c5, c6), which is to say the person in the building least able to detect a wrong answer, because not knowing the answer is precisely why they asked. A reviewer only catches errors when they hold independent knowledge, and here they explicitly do not. Under a check-in queue they will read the top line and repeat it. The loop is real for CONSEQUENCE, a supervisor and a 24/7 desk are on site (c12), and weak for DETECTION. The downscoped Desk Search fixes this structurally rather than by trust, because a wrongly matched card is visibly about the wrong thing while a wrongly composed sentence is not.
cost_of_error_headline.study_must_state: The Texas A&M study measured GUEST-FACING chatbots, so applying it to a staff-mediated channel is OUR INFERENCE and not a measured finding. The study must say so.
answer_book_guardrails: Every card carries a source, a date range and a last-reviewed date
Rate and cancellation cards hold verbatim policy text only (c9, c10, c13)
A named owner and a review tied to the published season boundaries (c14, c16, c19)
Cards expire visibly rather than silently going stale

data_readiness.corpus_exists: The public half exists and is unusually good, small, bounded, permissioned and in the company's own voice. The half that decides whether the build is worth anything is unverified in existence, format and ownership.
data_readiness.what_is_public: Check-in and check-out (c8), cancellation notice (c13), summer late check-out rule (c7), third-party pricing (c10), 24/7 desks (c12), guest-initiated shuttle calls (c11), the van and its group exclusion (c17, c18), aurora wakeup call and headlamps (c19), the Golden Bear window (c16), the Aurora Season Special dates (c14), the direct booking line (c9), and the three addresses and routing paths (c1, c2, c3, c4). Perhaps a hundred cards worth, and cheap to canonicalise.
data_readiness.what_is_not_public_and_matters: Three things, and together they are LARGER than the public set. One, the operational long tail a desk actually gets asked, parking, pets, luggage hold, accessible rooms, plug-in outlets, maintenance escalation at 2am, what to do when the van is full. Nothing verified says any of that is written down. Two, internal SOP and training material, whose existence, format and owner are an open unknown, so it may be in PDFs, in a binder, or in one veteran's head, and if it is in a head then transcribing it is the project. Three, and this is the line neither candidate drew, THE CORPUS CAN ONLY EVER HOLD POLICY, NEVER STATE. Nothing verified names a property management, booking or messaging system, so no live availability, rate or room status can be in it. Every question whose answer changes hourly is permanently out of scope, and that is a large share of desk traffic. The addressable question set is smaller than the pitch implies and the study must say so.
data_readiness.freshness_owner: Unnamed and unverified. The proof this is live rather than hypothetical is on their own site, aurora season dated August 21 to April 21 on the Wedgewood special (c14) and mid-August to late April on the Bear Lodge rooms page (c19). That is a normal artifact of many pages over many years, NOT a sign of a company in trouble, and it is why a named owner and a review cadence are day-one line items.
data_readiness.is_the_data_gap_the_real_project: Yes, and it is also the good news. The editorial work of agreeing one correct answer per question, splitting it by property and season, and naming an owner IS the deliverable. It must exist before any retrieval layer could work, because pointing search at the uncanonicalised pile would reproduce the aurora date contradiction with a confident voice attached, which is worse than the contradiction.

compounding_error.step_count: SEVEN model-touched steps as written: interpret the question, decide the property, resolve the season, retrieve candidates, rank and select, compose a plain-language answer, attach the correct citation to that composed answer. Dictation adds a speech recognition step on a busy summer front desk, which is the first thing to cut.
compounding_error.math: Using the ILLUSTRATIVE per-step figures in AI_SCOPING, which are NOT measurements of this company, seven steps at 95 percent lands near 70 percent end to end and at 90 percent near 48 percent. Roughly one answer in three wrong somewhere, handed to the person least able to notice. The downscoped Desk Search removes four of those steps by construction, property is a login setting and the season is the date, both deterministic and therefore correct by definition, and it removes composition entirely. One model-touched step means end to end sits at the single-step reliability, and the residual failure is a visibly wrong card rather than a fluent wrong sentence.
compounding_error.conclusion: The compounding math ALONE downscopes this build. Anyone can check the arithmetic, which is the point of showing it.

habit_test.does_it_beat_turning_your_head: For a clerk standing next to a veteran, NO. Nothing beats that, and pretending otherwise would be the dishonest part of this study. The desk is staffed around the clock (c12), so asking is genuinely easy and it is also socially correct.
habit_test.honest_answer: What a build can beat is the three cases where turning your head fails. The veteran is on the phone, in the back, or is himself a seasonal hire that week, since the company more than doubles hotel staffing for summer (c5) and the roster it names is the front of house itself (c6). The second thing it beats is the uncounted cost, which is the interruption landing on the most experienced person on shift, over and over, on questions the FAQ already answers. That cost is real and nobody measures it. The design consequence is blunt. If the tool is slower than asking, it will not be used, so speed and being in a pocket matter more than answer quality, which is another argument against a generation step that adds latency to be less trustworthy. THE MOST HONEST OBSERVATION: the highest-adoption artifact here is probably not a search box at all. It is the printable shift sheet, the twenty questions that make up most of the traffic, on paper, taped to the desk, reprinted when the season flips on August 21 (c14). Paper beats a search box and it beats turning your head, and any study that will not say that has not earned the part where software helps.

composite_question_test.is_it_real: The mechanism is real and the anecdote is INVENTED. A 1am rail arrival for a party of twelve is a legitimate composition of four verified facts (c11, c17, c18, c8), so it is not fabricated. Its FREQUENCY is entirely unevidenced, and frequency is the whole argument. One constructed scenario was carrying the entire justification for the AI layer, which is exactly the shape of reasoning this gate exists to stop. Worse for the argument, if these composites recur they are authorable as scenario cards, so a real composite problem argues for MORE EDITORIAL WORK at the rules rung rather than for generation.
composite_question_test.how_we_would_know_before_building: The measurement is free once phase one exists, because a search box logs its own misses. Two numbers decide it. Zero-result and abandoned queries, and searched-then-escalated-anyway, each tagged by a supervisor as a lookup, a paraphrase or a genuine composite. Run it through the August 21 season flip (c14) and into the shoulder weeks around the Golden Bear closing in mid-September (c16). Before a line of code, ask the veterans and the supervisors what they get asked at 1am, which costs one conversation.

fatal_unknown.what: Whether the seasonal front-of-house roster is mostly RETURNING staff or mostly first-time hires. The company says it more than doubles hotel staffing for summer (c5) and publishes no split.
fatal_unknown.is_it_fatal: Fatal to the Copilot's justification, SURVIVABLE for the Answer Book. If the roster is largely returning, time-to-competence collapses as a framing and any onboarding-days ROI goes with it. Three things still stand even then. Returning staff return after roughly eight months away and across a product switch between summer and aurora season, so recall is a real problem for them too. The aurora date inconsistency (c14 versus c19) is a content defect regardless of who reads it. A canonical answer set still serves year-round staff and whoever works the general inbox (c3). The honest statement is that this unknown RESIZES THE PRIZE SHARPLY AND DOES NOT ZERO IT.
fatal_unknown.cheapest_way_to_retire_it: One question in the first conversation, BEFORE anything is scoped or priced. Of the front-of-house people you bring on for summer, roughly what share worked a season with you before. They can pull it from rehire flags in payroll in an afternoon. Cost is zero, it takes an email, and it must be asked before the engagement is priced rather than discovered during phase one. No study should be built on an unknown that one sentence retires.

buy_not_build.buy_from: An established housekeeping optimisation vendor, Optii being the one with independent evidence in this package
buy_not_build.why_not_build: Confirmed, with two additions. The evidence is the strongest in the package and honest in both directions (c36, c37) against (c38, c39). Buying is right because this is commodity capability with a working product, because MIT NANDA found buying from specialist vendors succeeded about twice as often as internal builds, and because building it would need per-attendant timing and live room status from a property management system nothing verified even names. ADDITION ONE, buy is not free. It needs integration and a housekeeping workflow redesign, which McKinsey names as the single biggest differentiator between the pilots that pay and the ones that do not, so the honest advice is buy the software, budget the integration, and pilot on one property before three. ADDITION TWO, we must NOT scale that EUR 13,800 to this company. The figure does not travel off its own property size and occupancy (c37), and the only room counts available are third-party listings (c20, c21, c22). Multiplying one hotel's measured saving by a DMO listing would be exactly the vendor-average-as-your-baseline move on the AI_SCOPING kill-list. Their own occupancy and loaded labour rate are the only valid inputs, and until they supply them the study quotes NO NUMBER.

buy_not_build.capability: Semantic matching over the answer cards, if the search layer is ever funded
buy_not_build.buy_from: An off-the-shelf embedding and search service
buy_not_build.why_not_build: A hundred cards is not an engineering problem. Anything bespoke here would be selling effort rather than value, and the real work is the eval set and the guardrails, which is where the budget belongs.

recommended_pick.name: The Desk Answer Book, with the search layer named as a conditional Next that we will not price today
recommended_pick.why: It survives because it is the only candidate that clears the bar at the lowest rung, and because the strategist's own RICE table already said so at 4.05 against 2.1, nearly double. It fixes a defect anyone can see from outside before a model is involved (c14 versus c19). It is the data-readiness project any retrieval layer would depend on anyway, so it is not a compromise, it is the PREREQUISITE. It stays clear of both evidenced hazards by construction rather than by promise (c30, c5, c31). It has a dated proving ground sixteen days out at the August 21 season flip (c14). It matches what the company is, a forty year old independent (c26) whose counter-position against chain apps and mobile keys (c42, c43) is a human who is always right rather than a me-too app. ONE FRAMING NOTE THAT BELONGS IN THE STUDY: this is not a rescue. They already publish a codified FAQ and staff the desk around the clock (c12), and satisfaction was scored 4 rather than 0 for that reason. This is a small editorial upgrade to something they already do well, and it should be SOLD AT THAT SIZE.
recommended_pick.what_changed_from_the_provisional_pick: The name, the phasing and the generation step. The provisional pick was called Desk Copilot delivered on the Answer Book as a funded phase one, and its own text conceded the honest reading of the RICE table is that the Answer Book wins outright. Naming decides what the reader thinks they were sold, what the demo demonstrates, and what the ROI models, so a phase two that might never be funded was quietly becoming the headline. There is a concrete consequence in our own process, a study whose pick is named Copilot produces a demo that is an AI chat box, and the prospect takes away that we pitched a chatbot, which contradicts the study's own conclusion. The gate the strategist wrote is good and survives intact. What changes is WHICH SIDE OF THE GATE GETS THE NAME. Second change, if the layer is funded it is Desk Search and not a copilot, retrieval only, returning the company's own card verbatim, no generated prose and no dictation in v1. Third change, the returning-versus-new staff question moves AHEAD of the scoping conversation instead of sitting inside phase one.

where_we_would_not_use_ai: Most of this build has no AI in it, on purpose. The season switch is a date, so a rule handles it. August 21 is either past or it is not, a rule gets that right every time, and you can test it exhaustively. Which property a clerk works at is a setting, not a guess. The group exclusion on the courtesy van is written policy, so that is a rule too. Deciding the one correct answer to a question is editorial work your people do once, and no model should do it for you, because the answer has to be yours. We would not put a model anywhere near a rate or a cancellation outcome, even with a staff member in between, because that is the one place the research measures real damage. We would not build a guest-facing assistant at all. Your desk is staffed around the clock and you hire for caring, personal experiences, so a machine in front of a guest would work against the thing you are actually selling. We would not build housekeeping route software either, that one you buy, and the honest version of the evidence includes the reviewer calling the marketed return fiction while confirming the savings are real. The only place we would use a model at all is matching the words a guest actually says to the card that already holds your answer, and even there it shows you the card instead of writing you a new sentence. If your own logs say the search box was enough, we will tell you that and stop.
kill_list: Arrival Desk as a build now. The desk is staffed 24 hours by design (c12) so there is no unattended window, the group exclusion is a live human judgment (c18), a structured form does the deterministic part, and we are forbidden from sizing the call load (c46). Stays in Later as a form and a dispatch board.
Any voice agent, permanently. c12 removes the only justification and c30 says the highest-frequency call types are the worst place for model error.
The generation step inside Desk Copilot. Seven model-touched steps compounding to roughly 70 percent on illustrative figures, reviewed by a first-week hire who by definition does not know the answer.
Dictation in v1. A speech recognition step on a busy summer desk adds error and latency to the one thing that has to beat turning your head.
The NAME Copilot. It is a search box over a hundred cards and calling it a copilot inflates it, which is the mild end of the agent-washing AI_SCOPING names.
Any guest-facing rate, availability or cancellation assistant, written down as a permanent non-goal with c28, c29 and c30 as the stated reason.

Corporate and Extended-Stay Response Desk as a scoped build. Reach of one inbox, evidence of one homepage sentence (c2), analogue with no numbers at all (c41). Reduced to one question about volume and first-response time.
Building housekeeping route optimisation ourselves. Buy it (c36 to c39), and do not rescale one hotel's measured saving onto third-party room counts (c20, c21, c22).
Any use of the 40 percent unanswered-calls figure to size anything (c46). It appears in no model.
Any headcount figure. The 2018 range (c23) conflicts with the current employer listing (c26), so we use none.
